limits: WHAT THIS ESTABLISHES: that scripts/lane-serveability-check.sh classifies what came back from /api/generate by what it SAYS, not by whether the server answered. Five BAD responses, each measured or named in #895 / the gate's header, must be reported `dead` or `unreachable`: HTTP 500 carrying the server's own loader-killed text; HTTP 200 carrying an `error` field and no generated token; HTTP 200 carrying BOTH a `response` field and an `error` field (a server that ANSWERS and cannot serve - the shape served() exists to refuse); a connection closed with no reply (curl exit 52); and a connection reset at once (curl exit 56). One GOOD response - 200 with a generated `response` field - must be `serving`. MEASURED on 2026-09-28 (issue #1281), three mutations of the gate, each reported BLIND: (1) served() ignoring the `error` field - bad-200-response-and-error-field scores `serving`; (2) the no-response branch emitting `serving`, exit 0 - bad-connection-closed-no-reply scores GOOD; (3) any 2xx read as serving, served() dropped - bad-200-error-without-response scores GOOD. Mutation (1) SURVIVED the first cut of this control, which carried only an error-without-response 200: that body fails served()'s `response` test first, so the error-field test was never reached. The response-and-error case exists because of that survivor. TRANSPORT IS NOT EXERCISED. There is no model host and no network: run-case.sh puts stub-curl.py first on PATH as `curl` and answers the gate's real request from the case's files - a status and body, or curl's own exit code - with a fixed elapsed time. So this does NOT establish how the gate behaves on a real socket: timeouts at --max-time, slow cold loads, TLS, partial reads, or how real curl renders -w on each failure. It proves the CLASSIFICATION of responses, which is the part #895 got wrong. run-case.sh refuses to run if `curl` on its PATH resolves anywhere but the stub, so a real curl can never turn a case into a network probe; the stub honours only the flags the gate passes and records anything else as a refusal, which the runner reports as `cannot-run` with the gate's output WITHHELD - a stub that fell over would otherwise read as `unreachable`, i.e. as a detection. /api/version and /api/tags answer identically in every case (daemon up, model catalogued), deliberately: those are what the anchor trusts, so /api/generate is the only variable. It does not cover age mode (--check-age), the no-curl `unknown` branch, or the model-absent 404 path. UNAVAILABLE IS DECLARED FOR A MISSING python3 ONLY (#1117), because the stub is python; CI's image has python3 and no curl, which is exactly why the stub is used rather than staging a real curl (orchestrator ruling on #1281: a fetched third-party binary in CI is a supply-chain decision that does not belong in a controls change).

anchors.why: CONSTRUCTED from the check this gate REPLACED rather than from an earlier revision of it: before #895, /qwen:auto and /gemma:auto delegated when GET /api/version answered and GET /api/tags listed the model. That is registration, not serveability, and #895 measured it passing in ~13ms against a host whose loader was being SIGKILLed. The anchor asks only those two questions, in this gate's contract. MEASURED against every case: `serving` on all four BAD cases - it never reaches /api/generate, so a 500, an error-bearing 200 and both dropped connections are invisible to it - and `serving` on the GOOD case, agreeing with the gate there. Its blindness runs in the dangerous direction, which is the one #895 paid for: a lane reported usable that dies inside the delegated call.
